title: Separate product drift from measurement drift
description: Choose an incident and move from a top-line score to paired judge and matched-population evidence. Each lens holds another source of change still so the likely cause becomes more defensible.

lenses.label: Top-line only
lenses.detail: Compare the published scores without controlling any changed variable.

lenses.label: Freeze the judge
lenses.detail: Score baseline and candidate outputs with one judge and replay stable anchors across judges.

lenses.label: Match traffic slices
lenses.detail: Hold the evaluator stable and compare equivalent task, language, tenant, and risk mixes.

scenarios.label: Stricter groundedness rubric
scenarios.detail: The product is unchanged, but a new judge penalizes answers that omit inline evidence.
scenarios.headline: The score fell, but the product did not materially regress
scenarios.pairedConclusion: Stable anchor outputs lose six points under the new judge while candidate outputs stay within half a point under the frozen judge.
scenarios.matchedConclusion: A harder traffic mix explains another 1.5 points; evaluator drift remains the dominant cause.
scenarios.action: Recalibrate the new judge against qualified human labels, backfill paired scores, and avoid rolling back the unchanged product.

scenarios.label: Stale retrieval snapshot
scenarios.detail: A candidate route serves an older document index to long-tail support requests.
scenarios.headline: A large regression appears after the candidate route opens
scenarios.pairedConclusion: The same frozen judge finds an 8.5-point candidate loss on matched outputs, so the application path changed materially.
scenarios.matchedConclusion: Traffic mix explains only 1.5 points; trace joins isolate stale citations on the candidate retrieval snapshot.
scenarios.action: Roll back the affected retrieval route, preserve failed traces, and replay them against a repaired snapshot before resuming.

scenarios.label: New multilingual traffic mix
scenarios.detail: A regional launch increases difficult Arabic and French support requests without changing within-slice behavior.
scenarios.headline: The fleet average falls as the product reaches harder requests
scenarios.pairedConclusion: Matched outputs remain within one point under the frozen judge, weakening the product-regression hypothesis.
scenarios.matchedConclusion: Reweighting to the prior language and intent mix removes 5.5 points of apparent regression.
scenarios.action: Keep slice metrics separate, expand representative multilingual evidence, and improve the weak slices without calling the mix shift a product rollback.

scenarios.label: Duplicated failure events
scenarios.detail: An analytics retry writes negative feedback twice for one mobile client version.
scenarios.headline: A feedback-derived quality metric drops while task checks stay stable
scenarios.pairedConclusion: Frozen-judge and stable-anchor comparisons show no application or evaluator movement.
scenarios.matchedConclusion: Deduplicating by request identity removes the apparent four-point decline from the affected client cohort.
scenarios.action: Repair and backfill the event pipeline, annotate the measurement discontinuity, and keep product exposure bounded while validation completes.
